drhp.business: Swaraj Suiting Limited ("Swaraj", "SSL") was incorporated in 2003 and has evolved into an integrated textile manufacturing company engaged in Denim and Cotton finished fabrics and Cotton Yarn. The Company operates across multiple stages of the textile value chain, including spinning, warping, yarn dyeing, weaving, fabric processing and finishing, with manufacturing operations in Bhilwara, Rajasthan and Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh. Its manufacturing capabilities have earned the confidence of some of the world's most recognised apparel brands.

risks.note: Cotton availability and prices can vary with crop conditions, demand-supply dynamics and commodity-market movements.
Higher inventory and receivable requirements can increase funding needs and affect cash conversion; CRISIL has characterised the Company's operations as working-capital intensive.
Newly commissioned capacities require stabilisation and progressive utilisation to achieve intended efficiencies.
Large expansion projects involve implementation, funding, commissioning and ramp-up risks; the CRISIL rating rationale specifically flagged execution risk relating to upcoming capital expenditure.
Competitive intensity and changes in textile realisations can affect revenue and margins.
Currency, freight, trade policy and geopolitical developments may affect export demand and realisations.
Interest rates, credit exposure and funding requirements can influence financial performance.
Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental, safety, quality and other regulatory requirements.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Cotton availability and prices can vary with crop conditions, demand-supply dynamics and commodity-market movements.
- Higher inventory and receivable requirements can increase funding needs and affect cash conversion; CRISIL has characterised the Company's operations as working-capital intensive.
- Newly commissioned capacities require stabilisation and progressive utilisation to achieve intended efficiencies.
- Large expansion projects involve implementation, funding, commissioning and ramp-up risks; the CRISIL rating rationale specifically flagged execution risk relating to upcoming capital expenditure.
- Competitive intensity and changes in textile realisations can affect revenue and margins.
- Currency, freight, trade policy and geopolitical developments may affect export demand and realisations.
- Interest rates, credit exposure and funding requirements can influence financial performance.
- Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental, safety, quality and other regulatory requirements.
